messages:
maya: CI red on nightly-gpu/l40-smoke — master -> failing cublas init on L40 nodes, marking for triage

maya: job: https://ci.internal.redwood/run/CI-5234
maya: quick log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-16T07:02:11Z] load_library: /opt/cuda/lib64/libcublas.so.12: undefined symbol: cuGetProcAddress
cudaErrorUnknown: cuInit failed: symbol lookup error: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so: undefined symbol: cuGetProcAddress
CUBLAS initialization failed: cublasCreate_v2 returned CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR
```

cheng: that "undefined symbol: cuGetProcAddress" screams driver vs toolkit mismatch. which container image is this running?

maya: image: gpu-ci:cuda-12.1-ubuntu22.04, runtime on node reports DRIVER_VERSION=535.86.10
maya: but libcuda.so on the node is coming from /usr/local/nvidia/lib/libcuda.so (525.*) in the snapshot we grabbed earlier — looks like partial driver upgrade?

kyle: cc @ira on infra side — can you confirm node kernel module / driver state for l40-pool-5 (node dgx-l40-07)?

ira: looking now, pulling node state. If driver userspace and kernel module are out of sync you can get symbol resolution issues like this.

ops-bot: build CI-5234 rerun requested by kyle on l40-pool-5 (trigger id rerun-1765432145)

cheng: try a quick repro with the same image but on an A100 node (if available) to see if it's driver-specific. Also we should avoid another full bisect until rerun completes.

maya: kicked a manual run on an a100 fallback pool: https://ci.internal.redwood/run/CI-5235 (same commit, same image)

ira: dgx-l40-07 shows kernel driver 535.86.10 loaded, but /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so is a stale symlink to 525.89.02. guessing a partial rollout left old userspace libs behind. filing INFRA-1423.

kyle: thanks — infra change/rollback preferred over workarounds. if we must hotfix, we can set LD_LIBRARY_PATH to point to the correct userspace libs for the job container, but that's fragile.

maya: quick update: CI-5235 (A100) passed, CI-5234 rerun on l40-pool-5 still fails with same symbol error.

cheng: confirms driver vs userspace mismatch. Not a test/flaky failure. Recommend blocking L40 pool until infra fixes or mark nightly as transient. I'll add a note to the flaky label for the job.

ira: INFRA-1423: investigating automated rollback of userspace libcuda symlinks to match kernel module. ETA 30m. If we need immediate unblocking we can migrate the nightly off L40 nodes.

maya: leaving job queued to avoid noisy reruns. thanks for the quick triage. :raised_hands:
